children: Malaysia’s S&P Global Manufacturing PMI fell to 49.9 in September 2026 from 50.2 in August. This marked the first deterioration in operating conditions since May, as new orders declined for the first time in four months and at the fastest pace since June 2025, while production growth slowed further to its weakest pace in seven months.
Firms reduced input purchases for a second consecutive month, citing adequate inventories, limited product availability and weaker inflows of new business.
Supplier delivery times also deteriorated, with vendor performance worsening at the fastest rate in three months.
Employment provided a brighter spot, rising for a second straight month.
At the same time, input cost inflation eased for a fifth consecutive month to its lowest level since February, while output price inflation slowed to a seven-month low.
However, business confidence remained subdued, with sentiment toward the year-ahead outlook weakening slightly to a five-month low.

title: Malaysia Manufacturing Sector Contracts in September
